content.value_statement: Genomic interval projects need consistent preprocessing, embedding, and evaluation choices. This skill guides Geniml workflows for BED files, Region2Vec, BEDspace, scEmbed, and consensus peaks.
actual_capabilities: Select Geniml tools for Region2Vec, BEDspace, scEmbed, consensus peaks, and utilities.
Draft Python and CLI workflows for tokenizing BED files and training region embeddings.
Explain parameters for CC, CCF, ML, and HMM universe-building methods.
Guide scATAC-seq embedding workflows that integrate with AnnData and scanpy.
Recommend evaluation checks for tokenization coverage, embedding quality, and universe quality.
Use BBClient, BEDshift, tokenization, and search utilities in suitable analysis contexts.
limitations: Does not replace validation by a genomics domain expert.
Requires valid BED files, metadata, genome assemblies, and chromosome sizes from the user.
May require Geniml dependencies, PyTorch, StarSpace, scanpy, or other external tools.
Cannot prove biological significance without experimental design review and benchmark datasets.

use_cases.title: Build Region Embeddings
use_cases.description: Plan tokenization, Region2Vec training, and embedding evaluation for collections of BED files.

use_cases.title: Analyze scATAC-seq Cells
use_cases.description: Prepare scEmbed workflows for cell embeddings, clustering, annotation, and scanpy integration.

use_cases.title: Create Consensus Universes
use_cases.description: Compare CC, CCF, ML, and HMM methods for project-specific consensus peak sets.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: I have [BED files, scATAC-seq data, or metadata] and need [goal]. Recommend the Geniml workflow, required inputs, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Region2Vec Training
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Region2Vec pipeline for [number] BED files using [genome assembly]. Include tokenization, universe requirements, key parameters, and evaluation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design scEmbed Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a scEmbed analysis plan for my scATAC-seq AnnData file. Include preprocessing, tokenization, training choices, clustering, and quality checks.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Universe Methods
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare CC, CCF, ML, and HMM universe-building methods for [assay type]. Recommend parameters, tradeoffs, and validation metrics for publication-quality results.

output_examples.input: I have 200 ATAC-seq BED files and need embeddings for sample comparison.
output_examples.output: Use a consensus universe, validate tokenization coverage, train Region2Vec, then compare embeddings with clustering metrics and known sample labels.

output_examples.input: I need a universe for noisy ChIP-seq peaks from several experiments.
output_examples.output: Start with coverage cutoff for a baseline, then test CCF or ML if boundaries are uncertain. Evaluate region counts, sizes, and input coverage.

output_examples.input: I want to cluster scATAC-seq cells with Geniml.
output_examples.output: Prepare AnnData peak coordinates, tokenize cells against a matched universe, train scEmbed, store embeddings in AnnData, then run neighbors, Leiden, and UMAP.

best_practices: Build or choose a high-quality universe before tokenization.
Record genome assembly, parameters, random seeds, and dependency versions.
Evaluate coverage, clustering metrics, and biological controls before downstream use.
anti_patterns: Training embeddings before checking tokenization coverage.
Mixing genome assemblies or universes across related analyses.
Treating similarity search results as biological proof without independent validation.

faq.question: What data does this skill work with?
faq.answer: It works with genomic interval data, especially BED files, chromatin accessibility datasets, and scATAC-seq workflows.

faq.question: Can it help with single-cell ATAC-seq?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide scEmbed planning, tokenization, training, clustering, annotation, and scanpy integration.

faq.question: Does it run Geniml automatically?
faq.answer: It provides guidance and command examples. Actual execution depends on available tools and user approval.

faq.question: Which universe method should I choose?
faq.answer: Start with coverage cutoff for simple baselines. Use CCF, ML, or HMM when boundaries or states need stronger modeling.

faq.question: What dependencies may be required?
faq.answer: Common workflows may need Geniml, PyTorch, scanpy, StarSpace, chromosome sizes, BED files, and metadata tables.

faq.question: Can it evaluate model quality?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends checks for tokenization coverage, universe quality, clustering metrics, and known biological labels.
